outcome_evidence: The cloth starts spread out on the table (frame 0, overhead_cam and wrist_cam). The robot acquires and lifts part of it (frames 136–170), but subsequent movement gathers it into irregular overlapping bunches rather than a completed fold (frames 177–249, both cameras). After release, the cloth remains rumpled on the table through frame 395 in overhead_cam; wrist_cam also shows the uneven result at frames 295–305. This is a visibly unsuccessful folding attempt, not merely an outcome hidden by the recording ending.

failure_annotations.explanation: After establishing control of the cloth, the robot moves the held portion while the remaining fabric bunches and overlaps irregularly (frames 177–224, overhead_cam and wrist_cam). Continued movement does not align the cloth into a fold, and opening the gripper leaves a rumpled arrangement on the table (frames 243–249, both cameras). Possession was established; the visible failure is the folding manipulation, not a missed acquisition.
failure_annotations.recovery: Spread the cloth flat again, identify corresponding edges or corners, and lift and place one side over the other before smoothing the fold; human intervention is not inherently needed.
failure_annotations.severity_evidence: The cloth is rumpled but remains on the usable tabletop; no tearing, damage, or disturbance of unrelated objects is visible.
failure_annotations.resetability_evidence: A straightforward flattening and repositioning of the cloth would restore the starting arrangement; no repair or difficult retrieval is needed, and this reset could be performed by the robot or a person.
